prompt_shifted: For returns to physical stores in Tennessee in 1999, find customers whose total returns for a store were more than 1.2 times what the average customer returns for that store were in that period under the same conditions. Consider only returns where both the returning customer and the store are recorded (exclude any return missing either). Compute totals and the per-store average at the (return-customer surrogate key, return-store surrogate key) grain. Return one row per qualifying surrogate-key pair, but display only the customer's alphanumeric business id; this intentionally allows the same displayed customer id to appear more than once. Order by customer id; limit 100 rows.

For web and catalog sales for each calendar week sequence we want the ratio of each day-of-week's sales to the same day-of-week's sales in the next year, as eight values per row: first the calendar week-sequence number itself, then the seven day-of-week ratios (Sunday through Saturday). Each week sequence totals ALL of its days' sales (a week may span multiple years; do not split by year). Each ratio row has  each day-of-week sales divided by the same day-of-week sales in the week sequence 53 weeks in the future, rounded to two decimal places. Order by week sequence asc, only show in output week sequences that ever occur in 1999. (though ratios compare to ~2000 ranges)

For all items from manufacturer 277, looking only at store sales that occurred in the 12th month of the year, report the total extended store sales price grouped by brand and year. Output exactly these columns in this left-to-right order: the year, the numeric brand id, the brand name, and the total extended store sales price. Order the rows by year ascending, then total extended sales price descending, then numeric brand id ascending; limit to 100 rows.

Identify billing customers who generated positive value through all three sales channels — store, catalog, and web in both 1999 and 2000. A customer's annual value in a channel for a year is the sum, over that channel's sales lines in that year, of each line's extended list price minus its extended wholesale cost minus its extended discount amount, plus its extended sales price. A channel's rate of growth from 1999 to 2000 is that customer's 2000 annual value divided by their 1999 annual value. Return up to 100 customers whose year-over-year growth from 1999 to 2000 was stronger in the catalog channel than in both the store channel and the web channel. For each qualifying customer, report: the Customer ID (the stable business identifier, not the internal surrogate key), First Name, Last Name, and Preferred Customer Flag (as recorded on their 2000 store activity). A customer qualifies only if: they have activity in store, catalog, and web sales during both 1999 and 2000; their annual value is positive in 1999 for each of the three channels; their rate of growth from 1999 to 2000 in the catalog channel exceeds their rate of growth over the same period in the store channel; and their rate of growth from 1999 to 2000 in the catalog channel also exceeds their rate of growth over the same period in the web channel. Sort the results by Customer ID, then First Name, Last Name, and Preferred Customer Flag, all ascending with nulls first.

Report output channel entity performance by three metrics and two dimensions in rollup form as five columns in this order: (1) the channel type + channel ('web channel', 'store channel', 'catalog channel'); (2) the entity identifier prefixed by channel with one of 'store' (store channel), 'catalog_page' (catalog channel), or 'web_site' (web channel) (no space; raw concatenation, ex `storeABCDEF`, `catalog_pageABCDEF`, `web_siteABCDEF`; completely null when rolled up); (3) total ext sales; (4) total returns; (5) net profit after subtracting return-related net losses. The entity id for the final result is the return entity id for returns and the sale entity id for sales, merged into single column for aggregate results. Sales individually filtered by sales date between June 10, 1999 and June 24, 1999 and associated with non-null sale entity identifier; returns individually by return date in that same period and use a non-null return-side outlet identifier by grouping. An entity ID should appear if it had any sales OR any returns in the period (so an entity with only returns in filter set and no sales still appears; entities with no activity in the period are excluded). Report any empty gross sales, returns, or net profit as 0 rather than null. (rollup format reminder: subtotal rows by channel and a grand total row across all channels). Sort ONLY by the post-group output by channel label and entity identifier, nulls first for both! Return only the first 100 rows. An entity may show in both sales or returns or only one for the period; the channel/entity label must be populated even if it is only in returns or sales.

Find the states with at least 10 qualifying line items (a line item being one ticket + item combination) in May 2000 where the item current price is more than 1.2 times the average current price across the distinct items in the same category (use the item level pricing, not the sale price for the item). Consider only items whose category is assigned, and only customers who have a current address record. That address may have no state recorded — still include those customers and report them under a null state. Use the state from the customer's own current address record. For states meeting the line item cut off, return the state and that line-item count, ordered by the count ascending with nulls first, then state with nulls first; limit 100 rows.

For store sales in the year 2001, report the average quantity, average list price, average coupon amount, and average sales price for each item. Filter by the point-of-sale customer-demographic profile recorded directly on the sale (the point-of-sale customer-demographic record, not the customer's current customer-demographic record): female, widowed, '4 yr Degree' education. Also restrict to promotions where the email channel flag is 'N' or the event channel flag is 'N' (at this scale factor these flags are always 'N', so the clause matches every promotion). Order by item code (the item's business identifier); limit 100 rows.

For store sales in the 3rd quarter of 2000, report total net profit per store name. Restrict to stores whose ZIP code's first 2 digits match the first 2 digits of any QUALIFYING 5-digit ZIP. A 5-digit ZIP qualifies when its full five-digit value (not just its 2-digit prefix) appears in BOTH of two sets: (a) the curated list provided via the `zips` parameter (a comma-separated string of 5-digit ZIPs — declare `parameter zips string;` and split with `split(zips, ',')`), and (b) the set of 5-digit ZIP codes where more than 10 preferred customers (those with the preferred-customer flag set to Y) have their current address record. Order by store name; limit 100 rows.

A single output row with five numeric columns, one per quantity bucket: 1-20, 21-40, 41-60, 61-80, 81-100. Each column's value comes from the store-channel sale lines whose quantity sold falls in that bucket: if the number of sale lines in the bucket exceeds the bucket's threshold (631342, 98763, 743812, 27452, 601159 respectively), the column shows the average extended discount amount across those lines; otherwise it shows the average net paid across those lines. The reason table is not used for any computation or filter -- the result is just a single row, not a grouping.

For customers whose current address record is in one of the counties 'Murray County', 'Crook County', 'Union County', 'Sioux County', or 'Elbert County', and who made at least one store sale in the second through fifth calendar months of 2001 (February through May) and either at least one web sale or at least one catalog sale in that same February-through-May 2001 window (matched via the web-sale bill customer or the catalog-sale ship customer), we want to pull a breakdown using the customer's current customer-demographic record, including only customers that have such a current customer-demographic record (a demographic record must be linked to the customer; customers with no linked demographic record — which would otherwise appear as a single all-null demographics group — must be excluded). Group by each combination of gender, marital status, education status, purchase estimate, credit rating, dependent count, dependent-employed count, and dependent-college count. Output exactly these columns in this left-to-right order: gender, marital status, education status, customer count, purchase estimate, customer count, credit rating, customer count, dependent count, customer count, dependent-employed count, customer count, dependent-college count, customer count. The customer count is the same value every time it appears (six identical copies, each placed immediately after education status, purchase estimate, credit rating, dependent count, dependent-employed count, and dependent-college count, respectively). Order the rows by gender, marital status, education status, purchase estimate, credit rating, dependent count, dependent-employed count, then dependent-college count, in that order; limit 100 rows.

Among customers active in both store and web channels in 1999, find those whose web revenue grew proportionally faster than their store revenue from 1999 to 2000. "Revenue" here is the sum of (extended list price minus extended discount amount) over that customer's sales in the given channel in the given year. Include a customer only if they actually have sales in all four buckets - store in 1999, store in 2000, web in 1999, and web in 2000; a customer missing any one of these buckets is excluded entirely (do not treat a missing year as zero). Also require each customer's 1999 total in both channels to be positive. Report billing customer code, first name, last name, and preferred-customer flag (from the 2000 store record); ordered by those four fields with nulls first; limit 100 rows.

For web sales of items in the 'Music', 'Jewelry', or 'Shoes' categories sold between 2001-05-12 and 2001-06-11, report for each item its business code, description, category, class, and current price, along with the total extended web sales price for that item, and that item's extended sales price as a percentage of the combined extended sales price of all qualifying items in its class (i.e., within the same category and date filters). The percentage is the ratio multiplied by 100 (a value between 0 and 100), not a 0-1 fraction. Report one row per (item code, description, category, class, current price). Order by category, class, item code, description, then the percentage; limit 100 rows.

For physical store sales in the year 1998, return the average ticket quantity, the average extended sales price, the average extended wholesale cost, and the total extended wholesale cost across all qualifying sales. A sale qualifies when it satisfies one demographic-and-price clause AND one address-and-profit clause. The demographic-and-price clause requires that the point-of-sale customer-demographic records and the point-of-sale household-demographic records jointly match one of three combinations: divorced with 'Secondary' and per-unit sales price (the unit price, not the line-extended amount) between 100 and 150 and household dependent count of 3; 'U' marital status with 'Primary' and per-unit sales price between 50 and 100 and household dependent count of 1; or married with '4 yr Degree' and per-unit sales price between 150 and 200 and household dependent count of 1. The address-and-profit clause requires that the point-of-sale address record has country 'United States' and matches one of: states GA/MO with net profit between 100 and 200; states IA/NC/NE with net profit between 150 and 300; or states KY/GA/MN with net profit between 50 and 250.

Find (brand id, class id, category id) combination tuples (no null values allowed for any of the 3 keys) for items that appear in all three channels (store sales, catalog sales, and web sales) at some point during 1998 through 2000 inclusive. For any sale matching those tuples in December 2000, aggregate the sum of quantity * list price (don't use precalculated line totals) and count of sale line items (order + item id combinations) by lowercase channel, brand_id, class_id, and category_id. Compute the overall average of quantity * list price across all channels (use average; don't divide the sum/count, as we want to remove null computed rows), all items (not just our tuples) in 1998 through 2000. Filter to leaf groups whose per-channel sales total exceeds that overall average, then roll up only those surviving leaf groups by (channel, brand id, class id, category id) to return channel subtotals and a grand total. The overall average is not restricted to December 2000. Report channel (lowercase), numeric brand id, numeric class id, numeric category id, total sales, and total sales line-item count, ordered by those four grouping fields with nulls first; limit 100 rows.

For catalog sales in the 3rd quarter of year 2000, report the total catalog unit price (use the unit price, not the total sales price) grouped by the ZIP code of the buying customer's own current address record. Include a sale if any one of these holds: the first 5 digits of that ZIP code are one of 54975, 69532, 75804, 71087, 68877, 60169, 74289, 50411, or 56614; or that address's state is NC, IL, or MN; or that sale's per-unit sale price (the same single-unit price used above, not the line/extended total) exceeds 500. Order by ZIP code with nulls first; limit 100 rows.

Create two unique populations of orders - orders whose line items ship from more than one warehouse (so there exists another line in the same order shipping from a different warehouse) and that have no matching catalog return on the same order number. Then for catalog sales whose ship date falls between 2001-05-01 and 2001-06-30 inclusive, whose point-of-sale shipping address recorded directly on the sale is in KY (not the customer's current address record) via a call center located in 'Williamson County', and whose order id appears in both our target order sets - report the count of unique orders, the total extended ship cost, and the total net profit. Order by the order count desc; limit 100 rows.

For store sales in the year 1999 that were returned in the year 1999 or 2000 by the SAME customer sk, find catalog sales where the store customer sk matches the catalog billing customer sk and and the catalog and store item keys match whose catalog sale date falls in the year 1999 or 2000. Only match on recorded customer keys: the store sale, its return, and the catalog sale must each reference an actual, present customer — records with a missing customer reference must not be treated as matching. For items in this intersection (bought in a store in 1999, returned in 1999 or 2000, also sold to the same customer through a catalog in 1999, 2000) report per (item business identifier, item description, store state), separately FOR EACH of three quantity measures - the store-sale ticket quantity, the store-return return quantity, and the catalog-sale ticket quantity - that measure's own count, average, sample standard deviation, and coefficient of variation (stddev divided by average). So there are three separate counts (one per measure), three averages, three standard deviations, and three coefficients. Order by item business identifier, item description, then store state, all with nulls first; limit 100 rows. (Null stddev or coefficient values are expected if count is 1).

For catalog sales in 2000, restrict to lines whose point-of-sale customer-demographic record has male gender and 'Primary' education. Also require that the billing customer's birth month is March, April, May, July, October, or November; that the billing customer's current address-record state is KS, IL, MN, FL, WI, or SD; and that the billing customer has a linked current customer-demographic record. Report averages of quantity, the recorded per-unit list price, the recorded per-line coupon amount, per-unit sales price, per-line net profit, the billing customer's birth year, and the dependent count from the sale's point-of-sale customer-demographic record. Do not use extended list or sales amounts, and do not divide the recorded coupon amount by quantity. Weight every average once per catalog-sale line, whose grain is (order number, item sk), including the two dimension properties by first projecting them to that line grain. The literal ROLLUP hierarchy must be `(item code, billing-customer current-address country, billing-customer current-address state, billing-customer current-address county)` in that order: item code is the first rollup field and county is last. Output the four dimensions in rollup order—item code, country, state, county—followed by the seven averages. This output column order is different from the row sort: sort rows by country, state, county, item code, then the grouping indicators for country, state, and county; keep those indicators hidden and last. All order elements use nulls first. Limit 100 rows.

For items managed by manager 20, for store sales in December 2001 where the first 5 digits of the customer's own current address record ZIP code differ from those of the selling store's ZIP code, report — for each (numeric brand id, brand name, numeric manufacturer id, manufacturer name) combination — the total extended store sales price. Use the address on the customer record, not any address attached to the sale itself. Include all four of brand id, brand name, manufacturer id, and manufacturer name in the output. Order by revenue descending, then by brand and manufacturer; limit 100 rows.

For catalog sales of items in the 'Music', 'Jewelry', or 'Shoes' categories sold between 2001-05-12 and 2001-06-11, report for each item its business code, description, category, class, and current price, along with the total extended catalog sales price for that item, and that item's extended sales price as a percentage of the total extended sales price of all items in its class. The percentage is the ratio multiplied by 100 (a value between 0 and 100), not a 0-1 fraction. Report one row per (item code, description, category, class, current price), excluding null item codes. Order (all with nulls first) by category, class, item code, description, then the percentage. Limit 100 rows.
